title: Method & Madness
desc: Actors who went too far, directors who broke the rules & the shots that shouldn't exist

questions.q: For 'Cast Away', Tom Hanks gained then lost how much weight — with a year-long production break in between?
questions.a: He gained 50 pounds for the pre-island scenes, then production paused a year while he lost it plus more

questions.q: The 'Steadicam' was invented for which iconic 1976 film?
questions.a: Bound for Glory (Woody Guthrie biopic) — though most people associate it with Rocky or The Shining, both came after

questions.q: What is a 'oner' or 'one-shot' in filmmaking, and which recent film faked being entirely one shot?
questions.a: An unbroken continuous take. '1917' (2019) was designed to appear as two continuous takes with hidden cuts — 'Birdman' (2014) did the same trick earlier

questions.q: Christian Bale lost 63 pounds for 'The Machinist' then had to gain it all back plus more for 'Batman Begins'. How long between films?
questions.a: About 6 months — he went from 55kg to over 100kg

questions.q: What is the '180-degree rule' in filmmaking?
questions.a: An imaginary line between two characters — the camera should stay on one side of it to maintain consistent screen direction. Crossing it disorients the viewer

questions.q: The most expensive film ever made (adjusted for inflation) isn't a recent blockbuster. What is it?
questions.a: Cleopatra (1963) — roughly $340 million adjusted. It nearly bankrupted 20th Century Fox
An object or goal that drives the plot but is ultimately unimportant — the term was popularised by Hitchcock. The briefcase in Pulp Fiction is a classic example

questions.q: Tilda Swinton reportedly slept in a glass box in a museum as performance art. She also did what unusual thing for her role in 'Suspiria' (2018)?
questions.a: Played three roles including an elderly male psychiatrist — wearing extensive prosthetics. It wasn't revealed until after release

questions.q: Which film holds the record for most extras in a single scene?
questions.a: Gandhi (1982) — the funeral scene used around 300,000 extras, some of whom were paid and many volunteered

questions.q: What does 'mise-en-scène' actually mean and why do film students overuse it?
questions.a: French for 'placing on stage' — it covers everything visible in a frame: set design, lighting, costumes, positioning. Students overuse it because it sounds sophisticated and covers basically everything
